card.name: Hanter Dro
card.era: Traditional (declined mid-19th c.; revived in modern fest-noz)
card.tagline: Breton Vannetais chain dance, the 'half-turn,' paired with an dro.
card.profile: Hanter-dro (Breton, literally 'half-turn') is a Breton chain dance from the pays Vannetais (Wikipedia FR; folk sources). Unlike the 'arm dances' an dro and the ridees, it is held firmly and is a 'feet dance,' like the gavotte; dancers stand in a chain (traditionally alternating men and women) holding hands with arms held still, body turned slightly left. It derives from Renaissance branles and had become moribund by the mid-19th century, progressively supplanted by the larides that derived from it. Combined with an dro it produces the dans tricot (dans trikot); the laride de Kervignac is a particular Hanter-dro form of the Lorient/Hennebont area. It is danced in fest-noz to sung kan-ha-diskan or instrumental accompaniment.
card.insight: Often paired/alternated with an dro within the same suite (dans tricot), it is recommended as a beginner-friendly fest-noz dance because of its simple held step (Wikipedia FR; fest-noz guides).
card.image_significance: Half-turn of the Vannetais chain. A representative image shows folk dress and patterned partner or group figures — Brittany (Vannetais), France.
